entities.name: Raḍwān ibn Muḥammad al-Sāʻātī
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fakhr al-Dīn Raḍwān ibn Muḥammad al-Sāʻātī, known as Ibn al-Sāʻātī ('Son of the Clockmaker'), was a pivotal Syrian polymath who flourished in the late 12th and early 13th centuries, dying in 1230. A physician, high-ranking government official, and an accomplished horologist, he inherited and meticulously documented the legacy of his father, Muḥammad al-Sāʻātī, the renowned architect of the monumental water-clock at the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus. Raḍwān's significance stems from his critical role in preserving and transmitting advanced mechanical knowledge, placing him at the intersection of practical engineering, medical science, and administrative leadership during the Ayyubid era.

His most celebrated achievement was the completion of *ʿIlm al-sāʿāt wa-al-ʿamal bihā* (The Knowledge of Clocks and Their Operation) in 1203. This comprehensive treatise detailed the intricate mechanisms, construction, and maintenance of his father’s complex astronomical water-clock, which was a marvel of medieval engineering, featuring automata, planetary displays, and precise timekeeping. Beyond horology, Raḍwān served as a respected physician, likely practicing in Damascus and possibly Cairo, and held influential government positions, including roles under the Ayyubid sultans al-Malik al-ʿĀdil I and al-Malik al-Kāmil, thereby blending scientific expertise with political acumen.

Raḍwān's work ensured that the sophisticated horological knowledge of the Islamic Golden Age was not lost, providing an invaluable blueprint for future generations and influencing subsequent mechanical designs. His detailed descriptions, accompanied by diagrams, offered a rare glimpse into the practical application of theoretical mechanics and astronomy. The treatise itself became a cornerstone for understanding medieval Islamic technology, demonstrating the era's capacity for complex engineering and the integration of scientific pursuit with public utility and aesthetic grandeur.
